 One Full-Time Opportunity.

 Preparing or reviewing certain notes and supporting working papers to the quarterly and annual financial statements

 Post-Secondary Degree in Business, Finance or Accounting
 A professional accounting designation
 Experience working with IFRS

 Proficiency in excel and Microsoft Office Suite

This role has no direct people-leadership responsibilities.

 Lead the evolution of the service model as program scope, product design, customer journeys, and delivery decisions iterate. 
 Apply strong business acumen to assess each iteration for impacts to service experiences, capabilities, processes, roles, hand-offs, technology, data, controls, training, communications, and change readiness. 
 Define the requirements, gaps, dependencies, and decisions needed to operationalize the service model and achieve the target state.

 Service-impact assessments identifying changes to experiences, capabilities, processes, roles, hand-offs, technology, controls, and business readiness.

 Current Need
 The US Oncology Network is seeking a Lead Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to partner directly with business and operational teams to turn complex, high-value problems into validated AI-enabled solutions. This is a hands-on, business-embedded engineering role for someone who can work comfortably in ambiguity, connect business needs with technology, and rapidly move ideas from discovery to working prototypes.
 The FDE leads the front end of the AI delivery lifecycle. You will understand workflows, frame problems, assess technical options, build and test prototypes, and validate value with users. Once a concept is validated, you will define a clear production path and work with AI Application Engineering, Data Engineering, MLOps, architecture, security, compliance, and operational teams to transition the solution for industrialization and scale.
 This role requires strong software engineering judgment, broad technical fluency, and exceptional stakeholder engagement. The FDE role provides technical coherence from problem through prototype, preserves the intended business outcome, and ensures downstream teams have the context needed to deliver a scalable, governed solution.
 Key Responsibilities
 Embed with practice and business teams to understand workflows, user needs, operational constraints, pain points, and desired outcomes.
 Lead discovery workshops, workflow assessments, and problem-framing sessions with executives, physicians, clinical teams, revenue cycle leaders, operational teams, and subject matter experts.
 Translate ambiguous business needs into clear problem statements, testable hypotheses, technical options, prototype scopes, and measurable success criteria.
 Advise stakeholders where AI, automation, data, or workflow technology is appropriate and clearly communicate capabilities, limitations, risks, and tradeoffs.
 Design pragmatic solution approaches using approved enterprise technologies, architecture patterns, and available data assets.
 Build working prototypes, proofs of concept, and thin-slice solutions that test feasibility and enable meaningful feedback from representative users.
 Apply sound software engineering practices so prototype code, interfaces, and design decisions can be understood, reused, or extended by delivery teams.
 Use AI-enabled patterns such as retrieval-augmented generation, copilots, agents, semantic search, decision support, and workflow automation when appropriate to the problem.

 Collaborate with AI Application Engineers, Data Engineers, MLOps Engineers, architects, product leaders, security, compliance, and business SMEs to shape an executable delivery path.
 Define solution requirements, dependencies, and acceptance criteria for production delivery.
 Assess production readiness and document risks, decisions, and required controls.
 Lead solution handoff to engineering teams and support successful implementation.
 Drive reuse by capturing patterns, assets, and lessons learned across engagements.
 Contribute to FDE playbooks, prototype standards, reusable asset libraries, and delivery practices that improve speed and consistency.
 Mentor engineers in business discovery, problem framing, rapid prototyping, and technical stakeholder communication.
 Minimum Requirement
 Degree or equivalent experience and typically 8+ years of relevant experience in software engineering, solution engineering, solution architecture, technical consulting, enterprise application delivery, or digital transformation.
 Education
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
 Critical Skills
 8+ years of experience building, integrating, troubleshooting, or delivering enterprise software solutions.
 Strong hands-on full-stack engineering and troubleshooting experience across modern web applications, APIs, data, AI services, identity, security, and cloud infrastructure.
 Hands-on experience with React, Node.js, TypeScript, Python, and modern web application architecture.

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead.  About the team
 The Risk team builds trust, an essential ingredient for Stripe’s mission to increase the GDP of the internet. We make it possible for millions of businesses to access and use Stripe’s financial infrastructure while protecting our users, financial partners, and the broader ecosystem from harm.
 Risk sits at the center of our users’ and Stripe’s ability to grow safely. We help legitimate businesses access Stripe’s financial services, provide credit to creditworthy businesses, and increasingly help users manage their own risk. We also prevent fraud and financial crime, manage Stripe’s credit exposure, meet our obligations to regulators and financial partners, and enable Stripe’s product teams to launch and grow products safely. To do this, we set the policies and standards that guide how Stripe manages risk and develop the advanced AI, infrastructure, and product experiences that put them into practice for Stripe and our users.
 At Stripe’s scale—$1.9 trillion in annual payment volume, equivalent to 1.6% of global GDP, processed across millions of businesses—we face risk problems no other company has encountered. The opportunities and complexities are only growing as AI reshapes what is possible, Stripe expands its product suite, regulators raise their expectations, and we support more businesses in more countries.

 As a Staff Product Manager on the Risk team, you will lead cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives that fundamentally change how Stripe and our users manage risk. You will identify the most important opportunities that cut across Risk’s infrastructure and products, define solutions to our most ambiguous problems, and drive execution from early technical shaping through delivery and adoption.
 You will operate as a product counterpart to Risk’s senior technical leaders. You will shape infrastructure and product direction across Risk, connect work that would otherwise remain fragmented, and help product teams across Stripe build on Risk’s capabilities. You will remain deeply engaged in the work, helping teams navigate difficult technical and product decisions.

 Identify high-leverage problems that cut across teams, turn ambiguity into clear product and technical direction, and establish measurable outcomes.
 Lead major cross-Risk and cross-Stripe initiatives from initial shaping through delivery, adoption, and iteration.

 Partner deeply with engineering, data science, and machine learning leaders to shape architecture, data foundations, models, APIs, and product experiences.

You raise the ambition and effectiveness of the teams and product managers around you without needing to manage them.

 Experience working with globally distributed teams.

 At Acuity Insights, we’re strengthening our accounting operations, improving our systems, and finding better ways to work. We’re looking for an experienced accountant who can take on complex work independently and help us build a stronger, more effective accounting function.

You’ll also help strengthen the accuracy and reliability of our financial and business reporting, including recurring revenue metrics, while contributing accounting insights to budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
 You’ll work closely with our Controller and alongside a small accounting team, bringing the judgment to work through complex accounting questions, identify root causes, and see issues through to resolution. Your experience will also help strengthen the team through shared knowledge, guidance, and better ways of working.
 There’s plenty to improve and build. We’re preparing for a new accounting system, exploring automation and AI, and reducing the manual work that slows us down. You’ll have the opportunity to lead meaningful improvements while helping make our accounting processes more reliable and scalable.
 If you enjoy solving complex accounting problems, sharing what you know, and finding better ways to get things done, there’s a lot here for you to contribute.
 Before you apply: This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in Canada. We’re hiring for an existing, open position. You’re welcome to use AI thoughtfully when preparing your application and conversations with our team. Just make sure what you share reflects your own experience, thinking, and judgment. During live conversations, please don’t use AI to generate responses unless invited to do so. 
 The Work You’ll Do
 In your first few weeks, you’ll get to know Acuity’s business, current accounting systems, processes, and controls, working alongside our Controller and accounting team to understand how things work today and where we can improve.
 We’re working toward a five-business-day close, and you’ll play an important role in helping us get there.
 Own complex accounting work 
 You’ll own significant areas of the accounting cycle, including complex journal entries and reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, and audit support. You’ll also review reconciliations and supporting schedules prepared by the team, investigate unusual items, and ensure the close is complete and ready for Controller review.
 When accounting questions are complex or something doesn’t reconcile, you’ll dig into the details, investigate root causes, and use sound judgment to recommend the right path forward. Your work will help us build a faster, more reliable close supported by strong processes and controls.
 Strengthen revenue accounting and reporting 
 You’ll provide senior-level review and oversight of revenue accounting, including revenue recognition, deferred revenue, reconciliations, and related reporting. Working with teammates responsible for invoicing, receivables, and recurring revenue schedules, you’ll connect business activity with accounting records.
 You’ll review accounting outputs, investigate discrepancies, and resolve complex or unusual transactions. You’ll help ensure revenue is recognized appropriately, supporting schedules reconcile to the general ledger, and financial and business reporting is accurate and reliable..
 Turn accounting information into reliable financial insight 
 You’ll help ensure the accounting information behind our financial and business reporting is accurate, consistent, and reliable, including the preparation and reconciliation of recurring revenue metrics.
 You’ll contribute accounting insights and historical context to financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting, helping the business make informed decisions. You’ll also support cash management through short-term cash forecasting, cash flow variance analysis, and visibility into upcoming cash requirements.
 Help modernize our accounting systems 
 We’re preparing to move to a new accounting platform. You’ll contribute your accounting expertise to the transition, from defining requirements and improving workflows to data validation, testing, and migration.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take ownership of meaningful improvements that make our systems and processes more efficient, reliable, and easier to use.
 Improve how Accounting works 
 You’ll look beyond your own responsibilities to identify recurring problems, unnecessary manual work, and opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls, and use automation or AI thoughtfully.
 You’ll help turn those opportunities into practical improvements, while strengthening documentation, sharing knowledge, and building better coverage across the team.
 The goal is an accounting function that spends less time moving information around and more time on the work where expertise and judgment matter.
 Who You’ll Work With and How
 You’ll report to our Controller and work alongside a small team of accountants. You’ll have meaningful ownership of your work while sharing knowledge, solving problems together, and helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 Accounting connects to almost every part of Acuity, so you’ll work closely with people across the business:
 Your Accounting teammates , to work through complex questions, share expertise, strengthen coverage, and improve how the team works.
 Revenue Operations , to connect contracts, billing, revenue, and the information that supports accurate financial reporting.
 People & Culture , on payroll, employee-related accounting, and the processes that connect our teams.
 Leaders and budget owners , to understand the context behind transactions, resolve accounting questions, and support reliable financial information.
 External partners , including auditors and other Finance partners, to support reporting, compliance, and audit readiness.
 You’ll work with a high degree of independence, but not in isolation. You’ll know when to make decisions, when to bring others in, and how to build trust through clear communication, sound judgment, and reliable follow-through.
 What Success Looks Like
 In your first three months, you’ll build an understanding of Acuity’s business, accounting cycle, systems, and controls. You’ll begin taking ownership of key accounting responsibilities, building relationships across the business, and identifying opportunities to improve how work gets done.
 By six months, you’ll independently own significant areas of the accounting cycle, confidently work through complex reconciliations and accounting questions, and identify issues before they become problems. You’ll also begin turning improvement opportunities into practical changes.
 By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted source of accounting expertise, handling complex work with minimal guidance and contributing improvements beyond your own responsibilities. Your impact will be visible in stronger processes, better controls, and greater shared knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 How You’ll Succeed

 Take ownership. You follow work through to resolution, surface issues early, and take responsibility for accurate, reliable outcomes.
 Look beyond the numbers. You investigate discrepancies, ask questions, and connect the dots to understand what’s really happening.
 Balance judgment with momentum. You respect accounting standards and controls while knowing when to make decisions, move forward, or bring others in.
 Look for better ways of working. Y ou notice unnecessary complexity and manual effort, finding practical opportunities to improve processes, systems, and controls.
 Share what you know. You document your work, offer guidance, and help build stronger knowledge and coverage across Accounting.
 Use technology thoughtfully. You explore how systems, automation, and AI can improve your work, applying the same judgment and care you’d bring to any accounting decision.
 Are comfortable building while doing. You work effectively as processes evolve, bringing structure to your own work while helping strengthen how Accounting operates.
 As the Finance function evolves, you’ll have opportunities to deepen your expertise, take on broader ownership, and contribute to larger systems and process improvements.

 You’ll bring strong technical accounting expertise, sound judgment, and the ability to independently own complex work. Your experience will include:
 Independently owning significant areas of month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, working papers, and general ledger accounting.

 Steps in the Process

 ServiceCentral builds the software that runs product service after the sale: warranty claims, repair authorization, and service execution, for everyone from the local repair shop to the Fortune 50 OEM. We have been doing it for 25+ years. We are Dell's Partner of the Year, two years running, and our products run service operations across 1,200+ locations in 100+ countries. We are backed by Valsoft Corporation, a permanent-capital owner of 150+ vertical software companies, so we build for the next decade, not the next funding round.
 The Role
 ServiceCentral is hiring Partnership & Growth Associates to win new customers and grow the ones we bring in. This is a real sales role from day one: you will build your own pipeline, run your own discovery conversations, deliver your own demos, and carry a quota. New business is the priority here, and prospecting is not something you fit around the edges of your week, it is the heart of the job.
 You will also own accounts outright, which means you get to see the full arc of a customer relationship rather than one slice of it: winning them, getting them live, growing them, and keeping them. You will build real product depth, get hands-on coaching from people who have done this work themselves, and have experienced support in the room when a deal gets complex. What we are looking for in return is drive, curiosity, and a genuine appetite for hitting a number.
 What You Will Own
 Pipeline generation and conversion
 Generate qualified pipeline through outbound calling, email sequences, and social outreach across assigned campaigns, verticals, and territories
 Sustain consistent, high-volume prospecting activity as the anchor of your week
 Manage and qualify inbound leads with fast, accurate follow-up and correct routing
 Research accounts and stakeholders so outreach is personalised rather than generic
 Run discovery conversations using our qualification framework, and deliver online product demonstrations
 Close new business against a quarterly quota
 Hand off opportunities above your authority to Specialists, Managers, or Directors with full context, and earn sourced-pipeline credit
 Route opportunities on the other platform to your counterpart owner, and earn referral credit
 Account ownership
 Own the full commercial relationship for your assigned portfolio of accounts
 Maintain a defined contact cadence so no owned account drifts without engagement
 Execute standard renewals cleanly and on time
 Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, closing the simple ones and pulling in a Manager or Director on the rest
 Monitor account health signals and flag at-risk relationships early, before they become recoveries
 Execute defined save plays on accounts showing risk
 Onboarding and time to value
 Own commercial handoff and welcome communications that set clear expectations
 Coordinate onboarding with Solutions and Support so customers reach value quickly
 Track time-to-first-value on your accounts and intervene when it slips
 Act on or route expansion signals that surface during onboarding
 Revenue integrity
 Audit subscription billing on your accounts to prevent revenue leakage
 Monitor involuntary churn signals (failed and declined charges) and drive resolution within 24 hours
 Reconcile the billing platform against internal records so MRR reporting is accurate
 Verify plan changes (upgrades, downgrades, cancellations) are executed correctly before a customer notices an error
 Surface systemic billing patterns to your Manager rather than fixing the same problem repeatedly
 Enablement and team support
 Provide day-to-day support on larger accounts held by senior colleagues: routine maintenance, data updates, configuration changes, and low-complexity requests
 Absorb repeatable work so senior capacity stays on new business and strategic pursuits
 Create and maintain customer-facing Knowledge Base and self-service content that drives adoption and reduces inbound volume
 Verify release notes for accuracy and customer clarity before publication
 Support go-to-market materials and campaign content for upsell and cross-sell motions
 Support trade shows and events: booth materials, collateral, demo environment readiness, on-site coordination, and lead capture with follow-up
 Systems discipline
 Keep CRM records complete and current, with a scheduled next action on every open opportunity
 Log activity accurately, because your forecast and your credit both depend on it
 What We Are Looking For
 Commercial drive.  You want to carry a number and you want to beat it.
 Resilience.  High-volume outreach means high-volume rejection. You need to make the next call sound like the first one.
 Coachability.  This tier exists partly to develop you. The people who progress fastest ask for feedback and visibly act on it.
 Process discipline.  You will run recurring operational workflows (billing audits, cadence management, CRM hygiene) that protect revenue. Reliability here is the foundation of customer trust.
 Commercial instinct.  You notice when a routine support question is actually an expansion signal, and you do something about it.
 Clear written communication.  Your emails, customer-facing content, and CRM notes are all read by someone who will judge us on them.
 Customer empathy.  You will handle billing disputes and pricing conversations. Doing that well protects both the relationship and the revenue.
 Curiosity about the platform.  The Associates who become Specialists learned their platform properly, not just the pitch.
 Autonomy and Escalation
 You operate inside a structured playbook with a clear escalation path. Escalation is a strength at this tier, not a weakness.
 Decide yourself:  standard pricing and terms, routine renewals, day-to-day account management within cadence.
 Escalate: 
 Any discount request, however small
 Any at-risk account signal, immediately
 Billing discrepancies above defined thresholds
 Growth opportunities in your accounts that need a Manager or Director, routed with full context
 Requests for non-standard contract terms, service commitments, or SLAs
 Quota and Compensation
 You will carry a quarterly quota weighted heavily toward new business, with expansion and renewal making up the balance. Quota is set from your assigned accounts and territory rather than a generic benchmark, and it ramps across your first two quarters so you are not held to full target while you are still learning.
 Compensation is a competitive base plus variable, with the variable tied to new business won, pipeline quality, and team performance. We will walk you through targets, weightings, and exactly how performance is measured during the interview process.
 Where This Leads
 Associate is the first rung of a four-tier track. Typical progression to  Partnership & Growth Specialist  takes 12 to 24 months.
 To be promoted you will need to show: 
 Two consecutive quarters at or above quota
 Clean, independent ownership of your named accounts
 Ability to run discovery unsupervised
 Evidence you have informally coached at least one peer
 Compensation and logistics
 On-target earnings: $130k CAD  (base ~$50-70k plus variable). Variable is tied to closed-won new business. When our MD or CCO leads the close on an enterprise deal, you share in the win for the pipeline you built and advanced
 Full benefits
 Remote within Canada, with working hours that overlap Eastern Time, where most of our team sits. 
 Some travel expected, predominantly within North America

At Syntronic, we don't just follow industry trends—we set them! Join us in partnering with visionary companies and the brightest minds to turn ground-breaking ideas into reality. Imagine working on cutting-edge telecom advancements, pioneering automotive tech, life-saving healthcare innovations, and next-gen industrial automation. Our projects are diverse, impactful, and at the forefront of technological innovation. Be a part of something extraordinary!

Who are we?:
Syntronic is a global leader in design and development, specializing in electronics, electro-mechanics, and software. We’re not just a company; we’re a community of innovators. Our teams work on projects that define the future—from creating state-of-the-art communication systems and autonomous vehicles to advancing IoT solutions that revolutionize everyday life. At Syntronic, your work will make a real difference.

What we're looking for:
We are seeking individuals who want to:
·        Collaborate with top-tier clients on transformative, cutting-edge projects.
·        Engage with and learn from industry leaders
·        Innovate from concept to completion, ensuring high standards.
·        Gain international experience on global projects.
·        Thrive in an entrepreneurial environment that supports new ideas.
·        Explore multiple sectors like telecommunications, automotive, healthcare, and industrial automation.


We're looking for a highly motivated Mechanical Designer who designs mechanical systems supporting electro-mechanical products.
You will be involved in the development of mechanical design solutions for electronics products supporting Syntronic’s cross-industry customer base: Telecom, Industrial, Medical, Defense-Aerospace, Consumer, etc.
Minimum 5-8 years of applicable work experience, preferably in electronics product development

What you'll do : Develop, design and document mechanical assemblies and components including but not limited to fabricated metal components (milled, turned, stamped, and cast components), plastic injection molded components, and wire assemblies and cabling as needed.
 Development of solutions for electronics enclosures for thermal management, EMI/RF containment, interconnect, sealing and ruggedization to meet customer environmental requirements
 Development of solutions for printed circuit boards and assemblies (PCB / PCBA) for mechanical integrity, mounting, thermal management, EMI/RF containment, interconnect, grounding, etc.
 Develop, design and document manufacturing, manufacturing test, and assembly fixtures and contribute to writing the manufacturing documentation for these fixtures' implementation.
 Investigate and solve problems as it relates to mechanical functionality of components and assemblies.
 Write engineering change notices.
 Perform component research and recommendation.
 Assist with assessment of suppliers and supplied product conformance.
What you'll need to get the job done: Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering
 5-8 years of experience in mechanical design (Sheet Metal, Machined, Casting, Plastic Injection Molding)
 Excellent Mechanical CAD Design Tool skills (SolidWorks, CREO or equivalent)
 Strong organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills
 Ability to quickly learn and apply new concepts, technologies and solutions
 Ability to interface with various disciplines/functional groups
 Team Player with strong verbal and written communication skills
What will make us REALLY love you : Design Experience within Defence industry
 Experience with MIL-STD requirements and testing (MIL-STD-810H, MIL-DTL-901E, MIL-STD-461, etc)
 Ability to obtain and maintain CGP and/or Secret Clearance
 Hands-on experience with finite element analysis (FEA) for structural and vibration modeling (ANSYS/SW-Sim, etc), and thermal/CFD modeling (SW-FlowSim/Flotherm, etc) with the ability to correlate simulation outputs to empirical test results.
 Background in DFM/DFA for high-reliability assemblies, including collaboration with contract manufacturers to optimize tolerances, materials, and processes for defense-grade production.

About Us 
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.
 At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.
 Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.
 Job Description 
 Visa Consulting and Analytics (VCA) drives tangible, impactful results for Visa’s network clients, including both financial services and merchants. Drawing on our expertise in strategy consulting, data analytics, brand management, marketing, operational and macroeconomics, Visa Consulting and Analytics solves the most strategic problems for our clients. 
 We apply deep industry and specialized expertise  to help clients address their key business priorities, drive growth and improve profitability. The VCA team provides a comprehensive range of consulting services to deliver solutions that address unique challenges in areas such as improving profitability, strategic growth, customer experience, digital payments, and risk management. 
The VCA team is looking for a Manager to join our Digital Performance  consulting practice and play a role in developing high impact projects for Visa’s clients in the North America region. The potential candidate will be responsible for delivering and implementing projects and solutions with Issuers, Merchants, and Co-Brand Partners. This person will develop initiatives to promote sustainable and profitable growth through advanced digital transformation & innovative analytics. 
Potential engagements could include digital customer experience assessments, AI Strategy, Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), program launch, digital customer acquisition, customer and merchant life cycle optimization, retention enhancement, benchmark analysis, and profitability enhancement. 
Specific responsibilities include:  
 Develop frameworks, approaches, solutions and recommendations that effectively and efficiently address the most impactful opportunities and challenges, with a particular focus on digital related engagements  
 Build solutions and actionable insights that will help clients grow and achieve their objective  
 Partner with peers in other functional areas (e.g., merchant sales and solutions, marketing, sales, risk, innovation) and across global regional teams to execute projects in ways that leverage the breadth and depth of Visa’s resources  
 Produce insights, analyses and recommendations to improve client performance, boost growth, drive understanding of client issues and provide strategic guidance for client priorities across the verticals and segments with a specific focus on digital  
 Ability to effectively manipulate and analyze large data sets (industry and Visa) to determine meanings insights and recommendations for clients  
 Build scalable solutions, toolkits, best practice documents and consulting approach that can be applied across VCA practice  
 Incumbents applying for the role should be self-motivated, highly energized, detail-oriented individuals who will deliver strategic thought leadership, problem diagnostics and high impact solutions. Candidates must be able to develop strong working relationships with  external clients and across the Visa organization.   
 This is an individual contributor role, reporting into a Senior Director within VCA. 
Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager. 
 Qualifications 
 Basic Qualifications:  
 5 or more years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor's Degree or at least 2 years of work experience with an Advanced degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD)  
 Preferred Qualifications:  
 6 or more years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor's Degree or at least 4 years of work experience with an Advanced degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD)  
 Strong analytical skills, with demonstrated intellectual and analytical rigor  
 Self-motivated, results-oriented individual with the ability to handle numerous projects concurrently Relevant experience at a consulting firm, analytics firm, software development firm, or digital agency  
 Experience working with financial indicators to measure business performance. 
 Experience with advanced analytics & coding tools (PowerBI, python, etc)  
 Experience in developing & utilizing LLM tools to enhance productivity, including building LLM-driven agents & models  
 Experience in Answer Engine Optimization, including the building and use of custom tools  
 Knowledge of web analytics & digital measurement tools (Adobe, Google, etc)  
 Knowledge and understanding of banking operations and payments, including products and services, digital customer experience, marketing initiatives and card acquiring experience  
 Strong communication and presentation skills  
 Technology mindset, curious, up-to-date with digital trends and applications  
 Visa is an EEO Employer 
 Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

The Role
 At Treewalk, you'll run the day-to-day finance engine for the Indigenous governments, organizations and businesses we serve: clean books, a disciplined month-end close, timely funder reporting and year-end files that sail through audit. You'll own a portfolio of clients, acting as their fractional controller. Some will lean on you to keep operations running smoothly month to month; others will need you to get a backlog cleaned up and audit-ready. Either way, every file is yours to run.
 Deadlines are real; overtime isn't a lifestyle. We staff sensibly, treat extra hours as the rare exception, and back that up with true schedule autonomy and remote flexibility, so your evenings stay yours.
 If you've managed controllership or audit-prep engagements at a small- to mid-size firm, or run finance operations inside a First Nation, Tribal Council or Indigenous organization, and you're ready for high-impact work, tangible ownership and genuine balance, then we would love to hear from you.
 How You'll Create Impact Day-to-Day
 •         Run a disciplined close – Lead month-end and year-end close across your portfolio: reconciliations, accruals, deferred revenue, capital assets and journal entries, on time and review-ready.
 •         Keep operations humming – Oversee AP, AR, payroll and cash management processes, and step in hands-on when a client needs a fractional controller's precision and speed.
 •         Make audits painless – Build year-end audit files and lead schedules, prep airtight support, clear PBC lists and quarterback conversations with external auditors so leadership can sleep at night.
 •         Get the hard files back on track – Clean up backlogs and prior-year issues, so clients go from catch-up mode to a clean, audit-ready position.
 •         Run the engine of multi-entity groups – Keep the books straight across Nations' governments, economic development corporations, limited partnerships, trusts and societies, including intercompany and fund accounting.
 •         Keep funding on track – Track funding by program, manage deferred and restricted funds, and prepare reporting for ISC, CIRNAC, FNHA and other funders.
 •         Build strong controls – Design practical processes, internal controls and financial policies that hold up to auditor and funder scrutiny.
 •         Grow the team – Coach and review the work of accountants, bookkeepers and CPA students, and build checklists and templates that scale across clients.
 Result: clients see you as the calm, trusted voice who keeps their books clean, their funders satisfied and their audits uneventful, while you build deep, meaningful expertise without the grind of traditional public practice. 
 Our ideal candidate...
 •         CPA designation required.
 •         Significant experience in controllership, month-end close and year-end audit preparation, ideally with Indigenous governments, organizations or not-for-profits.
 •         Strong working knowledge of PSAS / ASNPO, fund accounting and funding agreement reporting.
 •         Experience leading engagements and supervising staff.
 •         A respectful, relationship-based approach and an understanding of Indigenous histories, governance and the impacts of colonization.

 Please mention these bonus skills if you have them
 •         Audit experience at a firm serving First Nations or public-sector clients

 •         Lived experience as a First Nations, Métis or Inuit person, or connection to Indigenous communities
 Why Treewalk Feels Different
 It's Treewalk for a reason: we invest in your growth, trust your judgment, and protect your life outside the ledger.
 •         No-Strings Learning Fund – We pay 100% of your CPA modules, annual dues, and any pro-dev courses you choose, and we'll never claw it back if you move on.
 •         Freedom Over Face-Time – Own your deadlines, shape your schedule. Hit a midday workout, do the school run; just bring the results.

 Who We Are
 Treewalk is Vancouver-born and scaling nationwide. Our Indigenous Services group runs the finance operations of Nations and Indigenous organizations and gets them audit-ready, so leadership can focus on their community's goals while we keep the numbers strong.
 But labels like "accounting firm" don't capture our DNA. Picture a tech startup powered by CPAs:
 •         Holacracy over hierarchy – Ideas outrank titles, and ownership lives on every desk.

 The Values That Power Us
 Mastery: We hunt knowledge relentlessly and build expertise into every engagement.
 Support: No one goes it alone; collaboration is our default setting.

 DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

 Efficiently operate the extrusion press while maintaining good quality that meets Almag’s quality standards.

 Die management - Ensure all necessary tooling is available at the beginning and throughout shift.
 Load dies into press and ensure presses are not waiting for die changes. Importance must be given to ensure dies are not loaded too early or too late.
 Ensure die temperatures are maintained when dies are loaded and removed from the ovens.
 Responsible for communicating directly with the team leads/maintenance team if any mechanical breakdowns or issues are encountered.

 Responsible for entering all downtime, die fails, quality issues, and schedule adherence notes in EPICS.

 Ensure sufficient spacing is kept between extrusion pieces on the cooling table to make sure proper cooling is maintained.
 Responsible for ensuring the extrusion is correctly fed into puller jaws. Notify maintenance/team lead if any issues occur.
 Ensure exit/runout temperatures are monitored and maintained throughout the run. 
 Maintain quality checks at front end of press during operation and continuously throughout the shift.
 Press samples must be properly labelled and kept together for traceability

 Complete press Ascona scans as required.

 Other duties as assigned.

 Technical Skills/Competence

veritree and Job Overview
 veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.
 veritree is seeking an Product Marketing Manager to own the commercialization of our restoration portfolio: turning every project we plant into a sales-ready package, and acting as the technical and impact expert our revenue teams bring into the room.
 We have active restoration projects across the globe, each one carries real depth, identifying the purpose behind the site, whether the trees are permanent or on a managed harvest rotation, the species mix and why it was chosen, survivability and monitoring data, the workers and communities involved, and the ecosystem returning around it. We need someone who can translate project details into one canonical source of truth, packaging it into narratives, value propositions, and assets our Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success teams can actually use, and then standing behind it on live calls.
 This role is a deliberate blend of product marketing, product ownership, and sales enablement. You will own the story of what we sell, not the marketing gloss, but the substantive, verifiable, layered version that wins enterprise deals. This is a storyteller's role first. You will be fluent enough in forestry, permanence, survivability, and our on-site technology to hold your own with a sustainability lead or a diligence team, but the reason we're hiring is narrative craft: the ability to make a Fortune 500 buyer feel what changes for a worker who once felled trees for income and now earns more, more securely, planting them.
 12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)
 Source of truth, live and trusted. One canonical project library covering 100% of active projects — purpose, permanence and harvest model, species mix, survivability, monitoring methodology, workforce and community context, ecosystem outcomes — current, maintained on an agreed cadence with Forest, and surfaced in internal materials for live call support.
 Every project sales-ready. A sales-ready package shipped for every active project: positioning, value proposition, proof points, pricing guidance, and customer-facing assets. No rep builds their own version from scratch.
 Impact story, three layers deep. A worker, community, and ecosystem narrative built and evidenced for our priority projects, backed by real data and media from veritree's technology — credible enough to survive diligence, specific enough to be memorable, and never greenwashing.
 Enablement that changes rep behaviour. Playbooks, proof-point libraries, objection handling, and training delivered so every Account Executive, Business Development Rep, and Customer Success Manager tells the same story, with adoption measured through call reviews and certification rather than assumed.
 Launch discipline. A cross-functional launch checklist and readiness standard, owned by you and adopted across Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, so nothing goes to market half-built.
 What You'll Do
 Source of Truth & Project Intelligence 
 You will build and own veritree's canonical library of project facts — one current, authoritative reference for every project we sell, replacing the scattered documents and tribal knowledge in use today.
 You will work directly with the Forest team to turn their intake into commercially usable intelligence: project purpose, permanence versus managed harvest and rotation length, species selection and rationale, survivability and mortality data, monitoring methodology, and site-level context.
 You will keep it current, with a defined maintenance cadence, clear ownership of each input, and version control the rest of the business can rely on.
 You will make it accessible where our teams actually work, surfacing project facts in Forge and our AI tooling so a rep can get an accurate answer during a live call, not after it.
 Packaging, Positioning & Pricing 
 You will translate every project into a sales-ready package: the narrative, the value proposition, the proof points, and the per-project assets that make it sellable.
 You will standardize delivery into ecosystem packages — mangrove, terrestrial, wildfire, agroforestry — rather than rebuild bespoke every deal, and you will own the product catalogue.
 You will own positioning across our growing solution portfolio, so that as we move from selling a single product toward solution-selling across multiple offerings and stakeholders, the story stays coherent.
 You will partner with Revenue and Finance on per-project pricing guidance and the commercial logic behind it, ensuring reps understand not just the price but why the project is worth it.
 You will own the change-flow when a metric is updated. When survivability, planting hours, or carbon updates, you push the correction into collateral, the portal, and CS on a set cadence — and you audit what's already in market.
 You will define which projects we lead with for which segments, and build the matching logic that helps reps put the right project in front of the right buyer.
 Impact Storytelling 
 You will build the impact narrative at three layers, and go deeper than the category norm on each:
 The worker — what this work actually changes for the individual, including the person who once cut and sold timber to feed their family and now earns better, more secure income restoring the same landscape.
 The community — how stable, better-paying restoration work compounds into local economic resilience, and what that looks like in the specific communities we operate in.
 The ecosystem — what returns to the site: canopy, soil, water, birds, wildlife, biodiversity — and how our technology measures and verifies it.
 You will ground every layer in evidence, using veritree's existing monitoring technology, field data, and media to turn claims into proof our clients can publish and defend.
 You will partner with Marketing to convert that depth into case studies, impact reports, campaign material, and event content.
 Sales Enablement 
 You will turn Forest's methodologies into sales-ready material — survivability, planting hours, social impact, carbon, permanence, verification — as defensible talk tracks, proof points, and objection handling. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one, and you only ever ship the defensible one.
 You will own the enablement library for project and impact content: playbooks, proof points, objection handling, discovery guidance, and competitive framing.
 You will design and deliver training and certification so every rep across Business Development, Sales, and Customer Success can tell the story consistently and credibly.
 You will review calls, identify where the story is breaking down, and close the gap with better material and better coaching rather than more documents.
 You will run a feedback loop from the field back into packaging, so what we ship next reflects what actually lands with buyers.
 Expert Support on Live Calls 
 You will act as the on-call project and impact expert, joining sales and Customer Success calls to explain projects in depth to prospects and customers when a rep needs the specialist in the room.
 You will handle the questions reps can't: permanence and additionality, survivability and replanting, harvest rotation and end use, monitoring and verification methodology, species and site selection, social impact measurement.
 You will represent veritree credibly in front of sustainability, ESG, and procurement stakeholders, and support diligence when deals require it.
 You will treat every call as a diagnostic. The goal is not to be permanently required on calls — it is to notice what reps couldn't answer and turn that into material and coaching so they can next time.
 You will not own the deal, carry a quota, or run the commercial conversation. The rep owns the deal; you make the rep formidable.
 Project & Product Launch 
 You will own the launch checklist and cross-functional readiness for new projects and new solutions — the definition of "ready to sell" and the gate that enforces it.
 You will own each project's availability, not just its launch — taking it online when it's ready and offline when it's sold out or paused.
 You will coordinate Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success through launch, so readiness is planned rather than scrambled.
 You will own the internal communication of what's new: what changed, what it means commercially, and what each team needs to do about it.
 Cross-Functional Partnership 
 You will sit at the seam between Forest, Product, Marketing, Sales, Business Development, and Customer Success, and you will be the person all of them come to for the truth about a project.
 You will feed field and buyer insight back to Forest and Product, influencing which projects we source, how we describe them, and what our technology needs to capture next.
 Requirements 
 Professional Requirements
 Exceptional storytelling and writing ability. This is the core of the role. You can hold a room, and you can put the same idea on a page without it going flat. We will ask for writing samples and we will read them closely.
 5-8+ years in product marketing, brand or content strategy, communications, or a comparable narrative-led role. Adjacent backgrounds are welcome — journalism, documentary, impact communications, science communication — if you can show the commercial application.
 A track record of packaging complex or technical subject matter into positioning, narratives, and assets that a sales team actually adopted — with evidence of adoption, not just delivery.
 Demonstrated sales enablement experience — building playbooks, proof-point libraries, and training programs, and measuring whether they changed rep behaviour.
 Comfort being customer-facing as the subject-matter expert: you can present with authority to an enterprise audience and hold up under informed questioning, without needing to run the commercial conversation.
 Genuine appetite for technical and scientific subject matter, and the discipline to represent it accurately. You know the difference between a compelling claim and a defensible one. You do not need a forestry background — you need to be the kind of person who will go and learn it properly.
 Experience owning cross-functional process — launch checklists, readiness gates, intake-to-market workflows — in an environment where that process didn't exist yet.
 Fluency with CRM and enablement tooling (HubSpot preferred) and a builder's instinct for using AI to make knowledge accessible at the point of need.
 Based in or able to work core hours in the PST time zone, and willing to travel to customer sites, planting sites, and the Vancouver office as required.
 Personal Strengths
 A storyteller by instinct — you notice the specific detail that makes an abstract claim land, and you reach for it before the statistic.

 We are seeking a Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help support the execution of lighting work across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on production role with opportunities to take on project-level leadership responsibilities. In addition to completing assigned lighting work, you may help coordinate tasks, review the work of other artists, provide constructive feedback, and ensure scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios to translate creative direction into lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, and performance.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, lighting pipeline, gameplay requirements, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, and other project disciplines.
 Create polished lighting work that meets the project’s established visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for assigned scenes, environments, sequences, or gameplay areas.
 Provide useful feedback and support to other artists when asked to review or coordinate lighting work.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and communicate them to the appropriate project leads.
 Deliver assigned work on schedule and respond effectively to internal and client feedback.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.
 Maintain visual consistency across related environments, gameplay spaces, sequences, times of day, and lighting conditions.
 Bring assigned scenes from initial lighting setup through final polish.
 Respond to feedback from Art Direction, project leadership, and clients in a timely and professional manner.
 Ensure completed work meets project requirements for quality, performance, organization, and delivery.
 Leadership and Quality Support
 Help oversee lighting work for an assigned scene, group of scenes, feature, or milestone when requested by project leadership.
 Review the work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting.
 Provide clear, respectful, and actionable feedback through written notes, live reviews, reference images, paintovers, or in-engine examples.
 Help ensure lighting work follows approved visual targets, technical standards, and project requirements.
 Communicate expected outcomes, priorities, and quality standards to artists working within an assigned area.
 Monitor the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that may require additional revision or support.
 Confirm that feedback has been addressed before work is submitted for senior, Art Director, or client review.
 Support junior or less-experienced artists with lighting fundamentals, engine workflows, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.
 Lead by example through reliable execution, clear communication, constructive collaboration, and professional conduct.
 Escalate unresolved quality, schedule, scope, or technical concerns to the appropriate senior artist, Art Director, or Producer.
 Planning and Production Support
 Work with Art Direction and Production to understand lighting priorities, tasks, estimates, and milestone expectations.
 Help break lighting goals into clear and manageable production tasks.
 Provide progress updates and communicate when assigned work is at risk of missing quality, technical, or scheduling requirements.
 Participate in daily reviews, art reviews, milestone evaluations, and planning discussions.
 Help prepare lighting work for internal reviews, client presentations, milestone submissions, and final delivery.
 Balance hands-on production responsibilities with review, coordination, troubleshooting, and team support.
 Adjust priorities when creative direction, technical requirements, production scope, or client feedback changes.
 Maintain accurate task status and documentation using the project’s production-management tools.
 Technical and Pipeline Responsibilities
 Work with Technical Art and Engineering to ensure lighting is visually effective, technically stable, and appropriate for the target platform.
 Follow established budgets for dynamic lights, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, global illumination, memory, and scalability.
 Identify and help resolve issues involving exposure, shadow artifacts, light leaking, reflections, volumetrics, bake quality, material response, and post-processing.
 Use dynamic, baked, stationary, or hybrid lighting approaches according to the project’s established pipeline.
 Profile assigned lighting work and make informed visual adjustments to meet performance requirements.
 Validate lighting across relevant gameplay cameras, display settings, hardware targets, times of day, weather states, and scalability levels.
 Follow project standards for scene organization, naming conventions, source control, documentation, and asset integration.
 Contribute to reusable lighting setups, templates, documentation, validation processes, and team best practices.
 Identify workflow problems and communicate potential improvements to senior artists, Technical Art, or project leadership.
 Cross-Discipline Collaboration
 Collaborate with Environment Art to ensure geometry, materials, composition, and set dressing support the intended lighting.
 Partner with VFX to integrate fog, particles, weather, fire, emissive effects, and atmospheric elements.
 Work with Design to ensure lighting supports navigation, player guidance, combat readability, objectives, and interactive systems.
 Coordinate with Character Art and Animation to maintain readable and appealing character presentation.
 Support cinematic lighting needs involving shot composition, continuity, exposure, character lighting, and narrative focus.
 Communicate artistic and technical concerns clearly to both creative and non-creative stakeholders.
 Work effectively with distributed teams, partner studios, external vendors, and clients across different time zones.
 Requirements
 Professional experience creating lighting for games, real-time projects, animation, visualization, or a closely related field.
 A portfolio or reel demonstrating strong real-time lighting work.
 Strong understanding of lighting fundamentals, including value, color, contrast, composition, visual hierarchy, atmosphere, exposure, shadow, and material response.
 Experience lighting gameplay environments or interactive real-time scenes.
 Understanding of how lighting supports mood, gameplay readability, navigation, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Professional experience using Unreal Engine or another modern real-time engine.
 Experience with dynamic or baked lighting, global illumination, reflections, volumetrics, exposure, color grading, and post-processing.
 Working knowledge of physically based rendering and material response.
 Understanding of basic lighting optimization, including light cost, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, scalability, and platform constraints.
 Ability to take ownership of assigned scenes and follow them through review and completion.
 Ability to receive, interpret, and implement artistic and technical feedback.
 Experience reviewing artwork or providing constructive feedback to teammates.
 Ability to identify work that does not meet an established quality target and communicate practical improvements.
 Ability to balance visual quality, technical requirements, production scope, and schedule.
 Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
 Ability to organize priorities, communicate risks, and follow work through to completion.
 Experience collaborating with multiple game-development disciplines.
 Ability to adapt to different projects, visual styles, engines, pipelines, platforms, and client expectations.
 Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a distributed team.
 Tools and Technical Experience

 Unreal Engine 5 or another modern real-time engine
 Lumen or comparable real-time global-illumination systems
 GPU Lightmass, CPU Lightmass, or comparable baked-lighting systems
 Real-time profiling, visualization, and debugging tools
 Photoshop or comparable image-editing software
 DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, After Effects, or comparable color and compositing tools
 Maya, Blender, 3ds Max, or another 3D content-creation package
 Perforce or another production source-control system
 Jira, Confluence, Miro, or comparable planning and documentation tools
 Expertise with every listed application is not required. We are primarily interested in candidates who demonstrate strong lighting fundamentals, sound production judgment, adaptability, and the ability to learn project-specific tools.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience working in co-development, outsourcing, consulting, or work-for-hire game production.
 Experience contributing to a shipped PC or console title.
 Experience working across realistic and stylized visual pipelines.
 Previous experience acting as a lighting point person, task coordinator, reviewer, or feature owner.
 Experience guiding junior artists or supporting teammates without formal management authority.
 Experience working with remote teams, partner studios, or external vendors.
 Experience owning lighting for a level, environment, sequence, or gameplay feature.
 Knowledge of Unreal Engine systems such as Lumen, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, volumetric fog, reflection systems, exposure controls, post-process volumes, and scalability settings.
 Experience with dynamic time-of-day systems, weather systems, destructible environments, or changing gameplay states.
 Experience lighting cinematics, characters, dialogue scenes, or scripted sequences.
 Knowledge of cinematography, photography, film lighting, camera exposure, and color theory.
 Familiarity with HDR displays, tone mapping, calibration, or accessibility considerations.
 Familiarity with rendering pipelines, shader behavior, and material development.
 Familiarity with Blueprints, Python, editor scripting, automation, or technical-art workflows.
 Experience creating lighting documentation, templates, benchmark scenes, or review materials.
 Portfolio Requirements
 Your portfolio or reel should demonstrate:
 Strong real-time lighting with effective composition, mood, color, contrast, readability, atmosphere, and scene cohesion.
 Work presented in a commercial, proprietary, or modern real-time engine.
 Clear explanations of your individual contribution, responsibilities, workflow, and production decisions.
 Gameplay lighting that guides attention, supports navigation, and reinforces the intended player experience.
 Effective integration between lighting, environments, materials, VFX, atmosphere, characters, and post-processing.
 An understanding of optimization, scalability, technical limitations, and production constraints.
 Examples showing ownership of lighting from initial setup through final delivery.
 The ability to work from concept art, reference, environment blockouts, narrative direction, gameplay requirements, or developing creative direction.
 Adaptability across different projects, genres, visual styles, or lighting conditions.
 We also encourage applicants to include:
 Day and night treatments of the same environment.
 Dynamic and baked lighting examples.
 Lighting created for different gameplay states, weather conditions, or times of day.
 Before-and-after comparisons showing how lighting improved readability, mood, composition, or performance.
 Examples of work reviewed or coordinated under your guidance, with your responsibilities clearly explained.
 Lighting guides, reference boards, benchmark scenes, review notes, documentation, or templates created for teammates.
 Please clearly identify your individual contribution to collaborative work.
 How to Apply
 A resume and portfolio or reel link are required.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


WHY THIS ROLE?

This role is for a highly experienced Back-End Software Engineer who wants to work on core systems that shape how the platform (Model Vault) operates. You will help define the architecture of the platform where reliability, security, performance, and simplicity all matter, and where many of the problems do not have off-the-shelf solutions.

Model Vault is Cohere’s inference platform for deploying and operating models securely at enterprise scale. The team owns the systems between a customer and the underlying AI infrastructure, including identity, deployments, metering, billing, security, privacy, and confidential computing. We are strengthening these systems as Model Vault grows, with the goal of scaling to millions of users and supporting some of the world’s most demanding enterprise workloads.



AS A SENIOR/STAFF SOFTWARE ENGINEER, YOU WILL:

 - Evolve and scale the backend systems that power Model Vault, including authentication and authorization, deployment management, billing, metering, and customer lifecycle.

 - Lead major architectural initiatives across identity, payments, usage systems, platform scalability, and other core product foundations.

 - Build highly reliable control-plane services for provisioning, configuring, scaling, and operating model deployments across clouds and hardware platforms.

 - Design APIs and distributed systems with strong guarantees around correctness, consistency, isolation, failure recovery, idempotency, and observability.

 - Build security and privacy into the platform architecture, including tenant isolation, least-privilege access, auditability, secrets management, encryption, and confidential computing boundaries.

 - Solve complex problems that span backend systems, cloud infrastructure, security, and AI inference, where conventional SaaS patterns are often not enough.

 - Drive projects end-to-end, from architecture and threat modeling through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration based on real customer workloads.


YOU MAY BE A GOOD FIT IF:

 - You are a strong backend engineer with excellent fundamentals in distributed systems, databases, networking, operating systems, and security.

 - You have strong programming fundamentals and experience building production systems in languages such as Go, Python, Java, C++, Rust, or similar. You write clean, maintainable, well-tested code and make thoughtful tradeoffs between simplicity, performance, and correctness.

 - You have designed and operated production systems where correctness, availability, security, and performance mattered at significant scale.

 - You can take ambiguous, high-impact technical problems, define the right architecture, and drive them through to reliable production systems.

 - You have strong systems-design instincts and understand concepts such as concurrency, consistency, caching, queues, rate limiting, backpressure, failure domains, idempotency, and graceful degradation.

 - You think deeply about security boundaries and understand authentication, authorization, identity, cryptography, secrets, tenant isolation, and how small implementation choices can create significant security risks.

 - You are comfortable reasoning across backend services, APIs, databases, distributed systems, and the cloud infrastructure they run on.

 - You are comfortable diving into unfamiliar codebases and debugging complex problems that cross service or system boundaries.

 - You care about the details of production engineering, including instrumentation, capacity planning, migrations, backwards compatibility, incident response, and safe rollouts.

 - You are comfortable challenging existing architecture and evolving foundational components when the system’s needs change.

 - You have a track record of taking technically difficult projects from an unclear starting point to systems that other engineers and customers depend on.




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.
We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.
 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.
 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.
 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.

 We’re on a mission to drive financial innovation and help businesses build financial experiences that feel effortless, connected, and customer-first. That’s where you come in.
 The Role
 We're hiring our Senior Data Engineer (Data / ML Platform) to stand up data engineering as a discipline at Flinks . You'll own the data and ML platform that turns models into reliable production services, harden the data models the business runs on and close the seam between our data scientists and the product teams. This is a high-ownership, greenfield-leaning role: much of this foundation is yours to build and own, not inherit.
 If you like being the person who makes data and ML production-grade - pipelines, serving, governance, reliability - and you want broad impact across a company's data, this is built for you.
 What You'll Do
 Own and evolve the data platform - the BigQuery warehouse, dbt transformation layers, Airflow / Cloud Composer orchestration and Pub/Sub ingestion that feed every model and metric.
 Build and operate the ML platform - training pipelines (Kubeflow on Vertex AI), model serving (FastAPI behind Vertex endpoints), CI/CD, containerization and typed contracts. Take operational ownership of model-serving infrastructure so reliability isn't carried by the data scientists alone.
 Harden and standardize the data models the business depends on - improving schemas, fixing data-quality issues and establishing trustworthy source-of-truth feeds.
 Establish data governance and observability - bring data that lives outside the warehouse under proper governance and build operational metrics for products that don't yet have them .
 Standardize how data engineering is done across product lines - patterns, tooling and pipelines other teams can adopt.
 Partner across data science, backend and product on the producer to consumer contract (models produced by data science, consumed/aggregated downstream, surfaced to clients).
 What You'll Work On
 You'll help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' financial intelligence products, supporting everything from transaction enrichment and categorization to risk and payments decisioning.
 Key areas of focus include:
 Building scalable data pipelines that process and transform large volumes of financial data. 
 Designing and maintaining reliable datasets, data models, and feature pipelines used by machine learning and product teams. 
 Improving data quality, observability, and operational metrics across our platform and customer-facing products. 
 Developing cost-efficient, high-performance data services and infrastructure that support real-time and batch workloads. 
 Partnering closely with Data Science, Product, and Engineering teams to enable new capabilities and accelerate product delivery. 
 Contributing to the evolution of our data platform architecture as we continue to scale our products, customers, and machine learning capabilities.
 Our stack
 Python, SQL, Bash 
 Google Cloud Platform (GCP) 
 BigQuery and dbt 
 Airflow (Cloud Composer), Pub/Sub, and Cloud Functions 
 Kubeflow, Vertex AI, MLflow, and FastAPI 
 Docker, Terraform, and Protocol Buffers 
 Azure DevOps 
 Grafana and GCP Logging

 Greenfield ownership — help build and evolve the data platform that powers Flinks' next generation of data and machine learning products.

 Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes Science des données, Produit et Ingénierie afin de permettre le développement de nouvelles capacités et d’accélérer la livraison de produits.
